Safinamide, which contains a fluorobenzyl motif, has absolute oral bioavailability of about 95% in both fasted and fed humans.
Rufinamide, a fluorobenzyl-substituted azole carboxamide, has about 85% oral bioavailability, especially with food.
Alfuzosin, an aminopyrimidine/quinazoline-type drug, has 49% absolute oral bioavailability under fed conditions.

Additional high-F contexts reinforce that structurally diverse small molecules in this transfer set exceed the 20% threshold: trovafloxacin ~88%, lemborexant at least 87%, meloxicam 91%, bumetanide ~75%, ketanserin ~49-60%, and diclofenac ~50%.
